label.fr: Salle de sport, yoga et coaching

expects.rule: Membership and class prices are published (or at least an intro offer with its price), with commitment and cancellation terms.
A first step for newcomers is offered and priced: trial class, intro weeks, visit or first consultation, with one button to book it.
The class timetable can be read without an account, filterable by club, class type and teacher.
Each location shows its address, opening hours and facilities (pool, sauna, changing rooms, equipment).
An FAQ answers what prospects ask before visiting: what to bring, level needed, cancellation, accessibility.
Coaches and teachers are named with a photograph and their qualifications.

traits: 5 of 8 put a newcomer step forward: trial class at 35 EUR and an intro month (Temple), 2 weeks for $59 (Yogamaya), a 5-step trial session (training BOXX), a trial session (Essor), a booked visit (Phive).
Only 3 of 8 show real prices on the home page (Temple, Essor, Yogamaya's intro offer); Core Atelier shows package cards with placeholder amounts, the others keep prices on a separate page.
3 of 8 state opening hours on the home page (Phive 06:30-22:00 in the hero, Temple, training BOXX per club); none of the 3 studios run by appointment do.
Booking lives in an account or app on 4 of 8 (Phive app, Casa Corpo on Bsport plus an iOS app, Core Atelier sign-in to book, Temple's own booking page); training BOXX and Essor use a form or phone.
3 of 8 are multi-site and name every club (Phive 5, Temple 5 with full addresses, training BOXX 3 with address, hours and phone each).

Strong single accents over dark or cream grounds: yellow #ffe000 with pink #ff004d (Phive), gold #c1a26c on #101010 (Temple), cream #f7e7de with brown #553623 (Core Atelier), teal #0b2a2b with sand #ebdbc2 (Yogamaya).

sites.name: Phive
sites.why: Premium club chain in Portugal: full-width photograph, 'It's not just fitness. It's living fully.', and the essentials as repeated hero lines (train every day, Coimbra, Leiria, Lisbon and Porto, 06:30am to 10pm); Sign up to a join flow, View all Clubs and Schedule a visit. Facilities listed (heated pool, sauna, Pilates studio), classes booked in the app. Yellow #ffe000, pink #ff004d, near-black #161003; PP Formula with Acid Grotesk; PT/EN. No prices on the home page.
sites.recognition: Awwwards Site of the Day, 2025-08-05 (also Developer Award, date not shown)

sites.name: Temple Noble Art
sites.why: Boxing gyms in Paris: top line 'Dès 80EUR le mois' with Découvrir & Réserver, headline 'Paris boxe ici.', Devenir Membre button and a Google rating of 4.8 from 1,700+ reviews. Prices stated (35 EUR trial, intro 95 EUR a month for 2 months, no commitment), five clubs with full addresses, hours, timetables per club, and a Calendly link for a phone call. Gold #c1a26c on #101010. French only.

sites.name: Casa Corpo
sites.why: Boutique studio in Munich-Bogenhausen with reformer, Pilates, barre, hot yoga, HIIT, café and spa: 'Welcome to Casa Corpo', a studio photograph with Book now, a header Book now, and nine offer cards each with its own Book Now to /booking. A banner explains the move to Bsport and what existing members must do. Find us gives the district and a map link. Prices on a Pricing page; no hours or phone on the home page.

sites.name: Core Atelier Pilates
sites.why: Singapore Pilates studio with classes of three: hero image with Sign Up Now, a press strip (Vogue, Time Out...), testimonials, member area (packages, bookings, waitlist states), and a private-session request form (instructor, time of day, days, contact by email, WhatsApp or SMS) with a 24-48 h reply. Cream #f7e7de with brown #553623. Package prices show as 'S$.00' placeholders and the address only as 'Appointment Only'.

sites.name: Yogamaya
sites.why: Yoga studio in New York: logo with the street address under it on every page, a scrolling bar for teacher trainings, illustrated GIF-style artwork (dancing yogis, a lady and tiger), an intro overlay '2 WEEKS for only $59'. Nav: Classes, Rates, Teacher Training, YMTV, Events, Studio. Phone, text number and email in the footer. Teal #0b2a2b and sand #ebdbc2, Dahlia display type. No booking button on the home page.

sites.name: AlpineCore
sites.why: Pilates in Geneva and Haute-Savoie plus mountain outings and retreats: 'Pilates & Montagne, Exercice haut perché' with a three-card carousel (classes, retreats, outings), group and private class cards each with a Planning link, a journal (recipes, layering advice) and Instagram. FR/EN. No prices, address or phone on the home page; booking only through the Planning page.

sites.name: training BOXX
sites.why: Semi-personal training gyms in Tokyo, Kawasaki and Osaka: logo and a 体験予約 (trial booking) button top right, headline naming the service, a four-image slideshow. The trial is explained in five steps (book by form or phone, no shoes needed, body-composition check, 40-minute session, feedback). Each club lists hours, address and phone; prices per club on /price/. Trainers, user interviews and FAQ in the nav.

sites.name: Essor Fitness
sites.why: Private personal-training studio in Ecublens near Lausanne: 'Coaching Sportif & Nutritionnel à Ecublens (VD)' with 4.85/5 from 60+ reviews, goals listed, two buttons for action and a trial session, both coaches named. Full prices (130 CHF a session, packs of 12, 24, 36, duo, nutrition) and insurance reimbursement stated. The trial buttons link back to the same page and the page ends with template questions.

avoid: Prices hidden behind 'contact us' or a sign-up wall, or package cards left with placeholder amounts.
A timetable that can only be seen after creating an account or installing the app.
Trial or call-to-action buttons that point back to the same page.
Stock photographs of models in generic gyms instead of the real rooms, equipment and coaches.
Opening hours and club addresses missing from the site, or one set of hours contradicting another.
Motivational slogans in place of what is offered, where, when and for how much.
Template FAQ or contact questions left unanswered at the bottom of the page.

sources.name: Keepme, The crucial role of gym FAQs
